title: THE CITY THAT WALKED AHEAD OF THE SUNRISE
deck: On Tessaly the sun rises at the pace of a walking person, and the city of Orrin Kell has walked ahead of it for four hundred years under a Rule that forbids it to stop or to divide. A rockfall leaves one crossing, through a canyon of the people the city once left behind. Illuminara will not carry the city over it; she has nine days to learn whose grief the Rule is made of.
shape: Six scenes run from the Prow to the far plain. The first sets the Rule, the rockfall, the shade that makes nine hours survivable and Illuminara's refusal to hold the city together by strength. The second is her long walk in step with sixty thousand people, and the vow made at a graveside. The third finds the Hollowers, their cisterns and their ledger of the Left. The fourth has Conductor and Warden read each other's dead aloud. The fifth is the Warden's invitation, the Council's vote with a rider the Left wrote and the Prow priced, and the one piece of physics that is hers to give. The last is the rehearsal in which the count fails and is recovered by people, the crossing, one hairline crack, and the dusk bell reading two ledgers.

scenes.title: The Rule on the Prow
paragraphs: *Prow deck, Orrin Kell, Tessaly · day one of nine, the dusk bell*

The sun on Tessaly came the way a tide comes over flat sand. There was no moment to point to, only the discovery that your feet were wet. Far behind the city the heat front lay across the rock like a pale seam. Ahead the sky was the colour of a healing bruise, and sixty thousand people walked toward it on twelve rails, at the pace of someone who is in no hurry and is not allowed to stop.
Illuminara had stepped onto the Prow an hour earlier with her light folded down to the glow of a held lantern. Nobody had stared. A city that walks learns not to turn its head.

**Wenna Thaw**  
The Gannet Rift line is gone. A hillside came down on the rails four days ago. We have one repaired crossing, and it runs through Hollow Town. To use it, Orrin Kell must be two cities for nine hours: the Heel one side of the canyon, the Prow the other, and nobody between.

**Illuminara**  
And your model says nine hours is safe.

**Wenna Thaw**  
The canyon lies on the dusk side of the ridge. Its shade keeps the sunrise off the floor a day longer than the Prow gets, which is the only reason nine hours down there is survivable. Dividing costs us an hour of margin. The long line round the Rift costs six days. I know the arithmetic. I also have three thousand names.
She did not explain the names. A rope-scarred hand lay flat on the rail post beside her, and the hand was not shaking.

**Illuminara**  
I could hold both halves together while they cross. Nine hours is not long for me. I wanted that said first.

**Wenna Thaw**  
And the day you are not here?
Illuminara looked down the length of the deck, where lamps were coming on car by car as the dusk bell passed along it.

**Illuminara**  
Then the Rule would be mine. It would be a thing I keep for you, and you would be a city that is carried. No. I would like to walk the line first, Conductor. Both ends. Before anyone draws a plan.

**Wenna Thaw**  
It is eleven kilometres.

**Illuminara**  
Then I had better start at the front.

scenes.title: In Step
paragraphs: *The twelve rails, Prow to Heel · night one, the long walk*

She walked it at the city's own pace, which was harder than flying. The rails ran under her boots in a low continuous hum, and the hum was not a machine. It was sixty thousand people lifting and setting down their weight in a rhythm nobody had taught them, the way a crowd on a bridge finds the same step and has to be told to break it.

Within the first hour Illuminara stopped counting and began to be carried by it. A girl on the ninth rail was asleep on her feet, held upright by the people on either side who had not looked at her and had not let her fall.
*It is not a crowd. It is one held hand, eleven kilometres long.*
She found that she was smiling in the dark with nobody to see it. It had nothing to do with her light or her strength. She was merely walking in step, and the city had let her.
Near the Heel the conductor's lantern came up beside her. Thaw had followed the whole way on the outer plank, stopping a hundred times to speak to a walker, and calling none of it a stop.

**Wenna Thaw**  
At the dusk bell we read twelve names. Every dusk since Marrow Pass. The list comes round again in two hundred and fifty evenings.

**Illuminara**  
The Standing.

**Wenna Thaw**  
The city halted at the Pass to bury its dead from the fever. One night's funeral. By morning the sunrise had taken three thousand of those who stayed to mourn. We ran, and in the running the rear cars were cut loose to lighten the line. That night we made the Rule. Never stop. Never divide. It was written by people who had just done both.
Illuminara walked a long while without answering. She had been told that the Rule was a regulation and had looked for a number in it. It was a vow made at a graveside.

scenes.title: The Left
paragraphs: *Hollow Town, Gannet Canyon · day three, noon in permanent shade*

The town in the canyon lived by cisterns the way another town lives by a river, cut into the rock in long cool terraces lined with clay the colour of a thumbprint. Warden Dov Arkady was walking the lowest terrace with a hand on the wall, as a man walks beside a sleeping animal.

**Dov Arkady**  
Every four years the city passes our rim and shakes the stone for a day. We have patched the cracks for a century. This time, I am told, it must come through.

**Illuminara**  
I am not here to tell you it is safe. Everyone has a model. I have come to ask what the cisterns are.
He turned and looked at her properly for the first time. Water moved behind the wall, a slow low knock like a heart under a floor.

She knew the knock before she knew why. It was the rail hum still in her boots, a half-beat behind it, the way two bells a street apart agree and then disagree. She said nothing about it. She had come to ask, and a thing she found for herself was not a thing to hand him as a plan.

**Dov Arkady**  
These were dug by the cut-loose. By the people in the rear cars. The ones who stood in the dark at the Pass and watched the lamps go on without them. They dug till their hands bled and found the first seam of water in the rock. Every drop my people have, they have because someone left. Do you understand that I am being asked to put it under the city's feet?

**Illuminara**  
I think so. I think you are being asked to be generous to the thing that cut you off, and you are being asked in a timetable.

**Dov Arkady**  
A timetable. Yes. We are a gap in it. We have never been a place.
A girl of about ten sat on the wall of the terrace with a long ledger on her knees, a pen tucked behind one ear.

**Kesa**  
That is the Left. Four hundred and six names. My grandfather started it and I keep it. Nobody from the city has ever asked to see it.

**Illuminara**  
May I?

**Kesa**  
You can read it. But you have to read it out loud. It is not a book if it is only looked at.

scenes.title: Two Ledgers
paragraphs: *The edge of the Gannet Rift · day five, the dusk bell*

She had thought for two days about the way to ask. At the edge of the Rift, where the city's last good rail ended and the canyon began, Thaw stood with the Standing's ledger and Arkady with the Left's. Between them the wind came off the cold side of the world and made the pages lean.

**Illuminara**  
I will not tell either of you what to do. I will ask only this, and it will cost you something. Each of you read the other's names. Aloud. Before any plan.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Mine are three thousand, and I read twelve a night.

**Illuminara**  
Then read his.

Thaw took the Left's ledger from the girl's hands. She read the first name in the voice of a woman checking a hinge, and by the ninth the voice had stopped being a rail voice and become a voice. The wind kept turning pages. Arkady stood with his eyes closed.
When she reached the end of the first page, he opened the Standing's ledger.

**Dov Arkady**  
Hesper Doyle. Anselm Doyle. Ruth Caul.
He read for a long time. Some of the names he stumbled over. He had not heard most of them in his life, and said them as if they were guests.

**Dov Arkady**  
I had always thought it was a rule. A rule is easier. You can resent a rule.

**Wenna Thaw**  
I was cutting you loose in my head for twenty years. I did not know you were counting.

Kesa, at the edge of the light with her pen behind her ear, took the Left's ledger back. She would not have lent it to anyone she did not already trust, and her face said so. The wind turned another page of each ledger, and neither of them closed it.

scenes.title: The Invitation
paragraphs: *The Council hall, Orrin Kell · day seven, the third bell*

It was Arkady who asked. He stood at the Council's open floor with canyon dust on his boots and a folded paper in his hand that he did not read from. Illuminara sat at the back on a bench meant for apprentices, because she had no vote, and she was glad of it. Kesa had come up the rail behind him with the Left's ledger held to her chest.

**Dov Arkady**  
You have never asked us for anything. You have only crossed us. Today I make the invitation. Orrin Kell may divide at Hollow Town for nine hours, and Hollow Town will lead the Heel through the canyon. Our guides at each switch. Lamp lines strung from the Prow side, so that neither half is out of the other's sight for one minute. Not a rupture. A guest night.

**Councillor Brisk Hale**  
Warden, I have sat on this Council thirty years and I have never voted to divide the city. Nor did my mother. The Rule is not a courtesy to be amended when a hillside falls.

**Wenna Thaw**  
It is not an amendment because a hillside fell. A man read three thousand names aloud at the Rift edge, in the wind, and I could not shut my mouth on his four hundred.

**Councillor Brisk Hale**  
My mother walked this city to the end of her life and never once looked back at the Heel. If I vote to divide it for nine hours I am telling her what she kept was a habit.

Nobody answered him. Hale looked at Illuminara on the apprentices' bench, and she shook her head very slightly, to say that she would not speak for either of them. But she was asked for the one thing that was hers, and she gave it plainly.

**Illuminara**  
Sixty thousand footfalls fall together into one hard note, and a cistern wall is a bell. I have walked both: the cistern knocks a half-beat behind your rails. If each rail walks a half-step behind the last, the note smears into a hum the clay can take. I can show your guides the count. I cannot make anyone walk it.

**Kesa**  
We can call the count from the switches. Like the ledger. You say it and everyone says it back. And put a rider on it. If a cistern fails, the first rail hours after the crossing go to our water carts, and the mending of the cisterns stays with the children of the cut-loose.

**Councillor Brisk Hale**  
First rail hours. Do you know what that costs, Warden? Our grain cars waiting a half-length behind a water cart for a week, with an hour of margin already spent. Say the price where the Council can hear it.

**Dov Arkady**  
Then hear ours. The first seam, the one dug by hand at the Pass, has never been opened to the city. For nine days after the crossing it is open to the Prow's water wagons, and our own terraces drink last. If a wall breaks, Hollow Town goes thirstier than you do. We will not be the only ones who pay.

The vote took the rest of the bell. It carried forty-one to nineteen, and a clerk wrote two plain lines under the Rule in her careful hand: that Hollow Town should sit on the Council, and that Hollow Town should mend its own water. Hale was among the nineteen. Afterwards he asked the clerk to keep his no in the record with his reason beside it, and then asked the Warden, stiffly, which end of the lamp line the Prow could spare him for.

scenes.title: Nine Hours
paragraphs: *Gannet Canyon, the rehearsal · day eight, the second bell*

They tried it on three rails first, with the count called from the switches by children and Hollowers. On the ninth rail a man read a name under his breath, as he did every dusk, and his foot fell where the old rhythm wanted it. The rail beside him fell with him, and for four steps the hum in the stone went hard and white.

Illuminara, on the cistern ridge, could only watch it go. She could not have reached those feet without taking them. Kesa was already calling. A Hollower on the switch below took the count from her and gave it back louder, and the ninth rail dropped a half-step, and another, until the hum smeared and held. Nobody turned to look at the woman on the ridge who had not moved.
*Gannet Canyon, the crossing · day nine, first bell to ninth*
Eleven hundred Walkers refused the Heel half and went ahead with the Prow. A rail-wright called Ansel Pike stopped at the rim with his tools on his back.

**Ansel Pike**  
I walked your Rule thirty years, Conductor. I will not walk it under another people's lamps.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Then walk it under your own. There is a rail free for you on the far plain.
He nodded to the rail and not to her, and went on.

The rest went down into the shade behind a Hollower with a lamp on a pole. Councillor Hale held the Prow end of the lamp line on the rim. At the third bell he turned his head and looked back at the Heel in the shade, the first of his family to do it, and he did not let go of the line for nine hours.

Illuminara stood on the cistern ridge with her light folded to nothing and her hands loose. The count came up from the switches in a child's carrying voice, and the rails answered one half-step at a time.
At the fifth bell she heard it. A thin dry sound in the third terrace, a seam of clay giving.

**Illuminara**  
Warden. Third terrace, east wall. A hairline.

**Dov Arkady**  
I hear it. Kesa, the clay!

They came with buckets and wet hands. Illuminara went down the wall and set her palm to the stone beside the crack, and held the rock still for the four minutes the clay took to set. She knew as she did it that forty pairs of hands and a bucket of clay would have done the same without her, and she stayed anyway, one pair among many. Nobody thanked her. They only said, *Hold, hold*, and she did.

At the ninth bell the last car of the Heel climbed out of the canyon with a Hollower on every switch and the lamp lines strung bright across the shade. Prow and Heel were one city again on the far plain, an hour behind the heat. Behind them, on the switch poles of the canyon, seventeen lamps stayed lit where Walkers had hung them and would not take them down.
The first cart onto the new rails was a Hollow Town water cart, and the Prow's grain cars gave it half a length, the way you give way to someone who has paid.

That evening the dusk bell sounded on the far side of the Rift. At the Council's table a new chair stood at the end of the bench, and Kesa sat in it with the ledger on her knees. Thaw read twelve of the Standing, and then she opened the other ledger, which Kesa had given her without being asked.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Hollow Town has asked me to read these at dusk, so that we will not be a city that forgot to count them. Twelve. Then twelve.

Illuminara walked at the back of the Heel, in step, with a ten-year-old's hand in hers that had been put there without discussion. Ahead of them the sky was the colour of a bruise healing, and the city was walking toward it all in one piece, with the left behind among the lamps.

critic_line: Illuminara learns that Orrin Kell's Rule and Hollow Town's refusal are grief held in opposite forms, then joins the two communities' freely chosen repair with one testable piece of physics, so the city crosses without being carried, the abandoned gain a permanent voice and both ledgers are heard.

translation_sl.title: MESTO, KI JE HODILO PRED SONČNIM VZHODOM
translation_sl.deck: Na Tessalyju sonce vzhaja s hitrostjo človekove hoje, mesto Orrin Kell pa že štiristo let hodi pred njim po Pravilu, ki mu prepoveduje ustaviti se ali razdeliti. Skalni podor mu pusti en sam prehod, skozi kanjon ljudi, ki jih je mesto nekoč pustilo za seboj. Illuminara mesta ne bo prenesla čezenj; devet dni ima, da spozna, iz čigave žalosti je stkano Pravilo.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov vodi od Kljuna do oddaljene ravnice. Prvi postavi Pravilo, skalni podor, senco, zaradi katere je mogoče preživeti devet ur, in Illuminaričino zavrnitev, da bi mesto držala skupaj z močjo. Drugi je njen dolgi korak z ramo ob rami s šestdeset tisoč ljudmi in zaobljuba, dana ob grobu. Tretji najde prebivalce Hollow Towna, njihove cisterne in seznam Zapuščenih. V četrtem Kondukterka in Varuh drug drugemu na glas prebereta imena mrtvih. Peti prinese Varuhovo povabilo, glasovanje Sveta z dodatkom, ki so ga napisali Zapuščeni in ovrednotil Kljun, ter eno fizikalno spoznanje, ki ga lahko prispeva Illuminara. Zadnji prinese vajo, na kateri se ritem poruši in ga ljudje znova ujamejo, prečkanje, drobno razpoko in večerni zvon, ki bere z dveh seznamov.

scenes.title: Pravilo na Kljunu
paragraphs: *Krov Kljuna, Orrin Kell, Tessaly · prvi od devetih dni, večerni zvon*

Sonce na Tessalyju je prihajalo, kakor plima prihaja čez raven pesek. Ni bilo trenutka, na katerega bi lahko pokazal, le spoznanje, da imaš mokra stopala. Daleč za mestom je vročinska fronta ležala čez skalo kakor bled šiv. Pred njim je bilo nebo barve modrice, ki se celi, šestdeset tisoč ljudi pa je po dvanajstih tirnicah hodilo proti njemu, s hitrostjo človeka, ki se mu ne mudi in se ne sme ustaviti.
Illuminara je uro prej stopila na Kljun, svojo svetlobo pa je zložila na sijaj pokrite svetilke. Nihče ni strmel. Mesto, ki hodi, se nauči, da ne obrača glave.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Proga pri razpoki Gannet je uničena. Pred štirimi dnevi se je na tirnice zrušilo pobočje. Imamo en popravljen prehod, ta pa vodi skozi Hollow Town. Če ga želi Orrin Kell uporabiti, mora biti devet ur dve mesti: Peta na eni strani kanjona, Kljun na drugi in nihče vmes.

**Illuminara**  
In vaš model pravi, da je devet ur varnih.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Kanjon leži na večerni strani grebena. Njegova senca zadrži sončni vzhod z dna en dan dlje kot na Kljunu, zato je devet ur tam spodaj sploh mogoče preživeti. Z delitvijo izgubimo uro rezerve. Dolga proga okoli Razpoke nas stane šest dni. Poznam račun. Imam pa tudi tri tisoč imen.
Imen ni pojasnila. Dlan, brazgotinasta od vrvi, je ležala plosko na stebričku ob tirnici in se ni tresla.

**Illuminara**  
Med prečkanjem bi lahko obe polovici držala skupaj. Devet ur zame ni dolgo. Najprej sem želela povedati to.

**Wenna Thaw**  
In tistega dne, ko vas ne bo tukaj?
Illuminara je pogledala vzdolž krova, kjer so se, vagon za vagonom, prižigale svetilke, ko je mimo potoval večerni zvon.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bi bilo Pravilo moje. Bilo bi nekaj, kar ohranjam za vas, vi pa bi bili mesto, ki ga nekdo nosi. Ne. Najprej bi rada prehodila progo, Kondukterka. Od enega konca do drugega. Preden kdor koli nariše načrt.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Enajst kilometrov je.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bo najbolje, da začnem spredaj.

scenes.title: V istem koraku
paragraphs: *Dvanajst tirnic, od Kljuna do Pete · prva noč, dolga hoja*

Prehodila jih je s hitrostjo mesta, kar je bilo težje od letenja. Tirnice pod njenimi škornji so neprekinjeno tiho brnele, toda brnenje ni prihajalo iz stroja. Ustvarjalo ga je šestdeset tisoč ljudi, ki so dvigali in spuščali težo v ritmu, ki jih ga ni nihče učil, kakor množica na mostu sama najde isti korak in ji ga je treba naročiti prelomiti.
V prvi uri je Illuminara nehala šteti in se mu prepustila. Deklica na deveti tirnici je spala na nogah; pokonci sta jo držala človeka na obeh straneh, ki je nista pogledala in ji nista pustila pasti.
*To ni množica. To je ena sklenjena roka, dolga enajst kilometrov.*
Ugotovila je, da se v temi smehlja, čeprav je nihče ne vidi. To ni imelo nič skupnega z njeno svetlobo ali močjo. Le hodila je v istem koraku in mesto ji je dovolilo.
Blizu Pete se je ob njej dvignila kondukterkina svetilka. Thaw ji je vso pot sledila po zunanji deski, se stokrat ustavila, da bi govorila s kom od hodcev, in ničesar od tega ni imenovala postanek.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Ob večernem zvonu preberemo dvanajst imen. Vsak večer po prelazu Marrow. Seznam se ponovi po dvesto petdesetih večerih.

**Illuminara**  
Ostali.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Mesto se je na Prelazu ustavilo, da bi pokopalo umrle zaradi vročice. Ena noč za pogreb. Do jutra je sončni vzhod vzel tri tisoč tistih, ki so ostali žalovat. Zbežali smo, med begom pa odklopili zadnje vagone, da bi razbremenili progo. Tisto noč smo sprejeli Pravilo. Nikoli se ne ustavi. Nikoli se ne razdeli. Napisali so ga ljudje, ki so pravkar storili oboje.
Illuminara je dolgo hodila brez odgovora. Rekli so ji, da je Pravilo predpis, in v njem je iskala številko. Bilo je zaobljuba, dana ob grobu.

scenes.title: Zapuščeni
paragraphs: *Hollow Town, kanjon Gannet · tretji dan, poldne v večni senci*

Mesto v kanjonu je živelo od cistern, kakor drugo mesto živi od reke; v skalo so bile vklesane dolge hladne terase, obložene z glino barve prstnega odtisa. Varuh Dov Arkady je hodil po najnižji terasi z dlanjo na zidu, kakor človek hodi ob speči živali.

**Dov Arkady**  
Vsaka štiri leta mesto prečka naš rob in ves dan trese skalo. Razpoke krpamo že stoletje. Tokrat, so mi povedali, mora priti skozi.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem prišla povedat, da je varno. Vsak ima svoj model. Prišla sem vprašat, kaj so te cisterne.
Obrnil se je in jo prvič zares pogledal. Za zidom se je premikala voda, počasno, nizko trkanje kakor srce pod tlemi.

Trkanje je poznala, še preden je vedela zakaj. Brnenje tirnic je bilo še vedno v njenih škornjih, to pa je zaostajalo za pol dobe, kakor se dva zvonova ulico narazen najprej ujameta in nato razideta. O tem ni rekla ničesar. Prišla je vprašat; kar je sama odkrila, mu še ni smela podati kot načrt.

**Dov Arkady**  
Te so izkopali odklopljeni. Ljudje iz zadnjih vagonov. Tisti, ki so na Prelazu stali v temi in gledali, kako se luči prižigajo brez njih. Kopali so do krvi in v skali našli prvi vodni izvir. Vsaka kaplja, ki jo imajo moji ljudje, je tukaj, ker je nekdo odšel. Ali razumete, da od mene zahtevajo, naj to postavim pod noge mesta?

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da. Mislim, da od vas zahtevajo velikodušnost do nečesa, kar vas je odrezalo, in to zahtevajo v obliki voznega reda.

**Dov Arkady**  
Voznega reda. Da. V njem smo praznina. Nikoli nismo bili kraj.
Na zidu terase je sedela približno desetletna deklica z dolgim seznamom na kolenih in peresom za ušesom.

**Kesa**  
To so Zapuščeni. Štiristo šest imen. Začel ga je moj ded, zdaj ga vodim jaz. Nihče iz mesta še nikoli ni prosil, da bi ga videl.

**Illuminara**  
Smem?

**Kesa**  
Lahko ga preberete. Toda brati ga morate na glas. Če ga samo gledaš, ni knjiga.

scenes.title: Dva seznama
paragraphs: *Rob razpoke Gannet · peti dan, večerni zvon*

Dva dni je premišljevala, kako naj prosi. Na robu Razpoke, kjer se je končala zadnja dobra mestna tirnica in začel kanjon, je Thaw stala s seznamom Ostalih, Arkady pa s seznamom Zapuščenih. Med njima je z mrzle strani sveta pihal veter in nagibal strani.

**Illuminara**  
Nobenemu od vaju ne bom povedala, kaj naj stori. Prosila bom le to, in nekaj vaju bo stalo. Vsak naj prebere imena drugega. Na glas. Pred vsakršnim načrtom.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Mojih je tri tisoč, vsak večer pa jih preberem dvanajst.

**Illuminara**  
Potem preberite njegova.

Thaw je iz dekličinih rok vzela seznam Zapuščenih. Prvo ime je prebrala z glasom ženske, ki preverja tečaj; pri devetem to ni bil več železničarski glas, temveč preprosto glas. Veter je obračal strani. Arkady je stal z zaprtimi očmi.
Ko je prišla do konca prve strani, je odprl seznam Ostalih.

**Dov Arkady**  
Hesper Doyle. Anselm Doyle. Ruth Caul.
Dolgo je bral. Pri nekaterih imenih se mu je zataknilo. Večine v življenju še ni slišal in izgovarjal jih je, kakor da so gostje.

**Dov Arkady**  
Vedno sem mislil, da je samo pravilo. Pravilo je lažje. Pravilu lahko zameriš.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Dvajset let sem vas v mislih odklapljala. Nisem vedela, da štejete.

Kesa, ki je stala na robu svetlobe s peresom za ušesom, je vzela seznam Zapuščenih nazaj. Ne bi ga posodila nikomur, ki mu še ne zaupa, in njen obraz je to povedal. Veter je obrnil novo stran obeh seznamov, nihče pa svojega ni zaprl.

scenes.title: Povabilo
paragraphs: *Dvorana Sveta, Orrin Kell · sedmi dan, tretji zvon*

Arkady je bil tisti, ki je prosil. Stal je na odprtem prostoru Sveta s kanjonskim prahom na škornjih in zloženim papirjem v roki, s katerega ni bral. Illuminara je sedela zadaj na klopi za vajence, ker ni imela glasu, in tega je bila vesela. Kesa je prišla po tirnici za njim, seznam Zapuščenih pa držala ob prsih.

**Dov Arkady**  
Nikoli nas niste prosili za nič. Samo prečkali ste nas. Danes vas povabim jaz. Orrin Kell se lahko pri Hollow Townu za devet ur razdeli, Hollow Town pa bo vodil Peto skozi kanjon. Naši vodniki bodo pri vsakem kretnem mestu. S Kljuna bomo napeljali vrste svetilk, da nobena polovica niti minuto ne bo zunaj pogleda druge. Ne razpoka. Nočitev gosta.

**Svetnik Brisk Hale**  
Varuh, v tem Svetu sedim trideset let in še nikoli nisem glasoval za delitev mesta. Tudi moja mati ni. Pravilo ni vljudnost, ki jo spremeniš, ko se zruši pobočje.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Ne spreminjamo ga zato, ker se je zrušilo pobočje. Neki mož je na robu Razpoke v vetru na glas prebral tri tisoč imen, jaz pa ob njegovih štiristo nisem mogla zapreti ust.

**Svetnik Brisk Hale**  
Moja mati je po tem mestu hodila do konca življenja in niti enkrat pogledala nazaj proti Peti. Če glasujem, da ga za devet ur razdelimo, ji s tem pravim, da je bilo to, kar je varovala, le navada.

Nihče mu ni odgovoril. Hale je pogledal Illuminara na klopi za vajence, ona pa je zelo rahlo odkimala, da ne bo govorila namesto kogar koli od njih. Toda vprašali so jo po eni stvari, ki je bila njena, in podala jo je naravnost.

**Illuminara**  
Šestdeset tisoč korakov pade skupaj v en sam trd ton, zid cisterne pa je zvon. Prehodila sem oboje: cisterna trka pol dobe za vašimi tirnicami. Če vsaka tirnica hodi pol koraka za prejšnjo, se ton razmaže v brnenje, ki ga glina prenese. Vašim vodnikom lahko pokažem ritem. Nikogar ne morem prisiliti, da ga hodi.

**Kesa**  
Ritem lahko kličemo s kretnic. Kakor seznam. Eden ga izgovori, vsi pa ga ponovijo. In dodajmo pogoj. Če cisterna odpove, gredo prve ure na tirnicah po prečkanju našim vodnim vozovom, popravilo cistern pa ostane v rokah otrok odklopljenih.

**Svetnik Brisk Hale**  
Prve ure na tirnicah. Ali veste, koliko to stane, Varuh? Naši vagoni z žitom bodo teden dni čakali pol dolžine za vodnim vozom, potem ko smo že porabili uro rezerve. Izrecite ceno, da jo Svet sliši.

**Dov Arkady**  
Potem slišite še našo. Prvega izvira, tistega, ki so ga na Prelazu izkopali z rokami, mestu nismo nikoli odprli. Devet dni po prečkanju bo odprt za vodne vozove Kljuna, naše terase pa bodo pile zadnje. Če zid poči, bo Hollow Town bolj žejen od vas. Ne bomo edini, ki bomo plačali.

Glasovanje je trajalo do konca zvona. Predlog je bil sprejet z enainštiridesetimi glasovi proti devetnajstim, pisarka pa je pod Pravilo s svojo skrbno pisavo zapisala dve jasni vrstici: da Hollow Town sedi v Svetu in da Hollow Town sam popravlja svojo vodo. Hale je bil med devetnajsterico. Nato je pisarko prosil, naj njegov ne ohrani v zapisniku z razlogom vred, potem pa je Varuha togo vprašal, kateri konec vrste svetilk mu lahko Kljun odstopi.

scenes.title: Devet ur
paragraphs: *Kanjon Gannet, vaja · osmi dan, drugi zvon*

Najprej so poskusili na treh tirnicah, ritem pa so s kretnic klicali otroci in prebivalci Hollow Towna. Na deveti tirnici je neki mož pod sapo prebral ime, kakor je počel vsak večer, njegova noga pa je padla tja, kamor jo je vlekel stari ritem. Tirnica ob njem je padla z njim in za štiri korake je brnenje v kamnu postalo trdo in belo.

Illuminara je lahko z grebena nad cisternami samo gledala. Tistih nog ne bi mogla doseči, ne da bi jih prevzela. Kesa je že klicala. Prebivalec Hollow Towna pri kretnici pod njo je od nje prevzel ritem in ga vrnil glasneje, deveta tirnica pa je zdrsnila pol koraka nazaj, nato še pol, dokler se brnenje ni razmazalo in umirilo. Nihče se ni obrnil k ženski na grebenu, ki se ni premaknila.
*Kanjon Gannet, prečkanje · deveti dan, od prvega do devetega zvona*
Tisoč sto Hodcev je zavrnilo polovico Pete in odšlo naprej s Kljunom. Tirničar po imenu Ansel Pike se je z orodjem na hrbtu ustavil na robu.

**Ansel Pike**  
Trideset let sem hodil po vašem Pravilu, Kondukterka. Ne bom hodil po njem pod svetilkami nekega drugega ljudstva.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Potem hodite pod svojimi. Na oddaljeni ravnici je za vas prosta tirnica.
Prikimal je tirnici, ne njej, in odšel naprej.

Preostali so odšli v senco za prebivalcem Hollow Towna s svetilko na drogu. Svetnik Hale je na robu držal konec vrste svetilk s Kljuna. Ob tretjem zvonu je obrnil glavo in pogledal nazaj proti Peti v senci, prvi v svoji družini, ki je to storil, ter devet ur ni izpustil vrvi.

Illuminara je stala na grebenu nad cisternami, svojo svetlobo povsem ugasnila in pustila roke sproščene. Ritem se je s kretnic dvigal v prodornem otroškem glasu, tirnice pa so odgovarjale druga za drugo, vsaka pol koraka pozneje.
Ob petem zvonu ga je zaslišala. Tanek, suh zvok na tretji terasi, glineni šiv, ki popušča.

**Illuminara**  
Varuh. Tretja terasa, vzhodni zid. Lasasta razpoka.

**Dov Arkady**  
Slišim jo. Kesa, glino!

Prišli so z vedri in mokrimi rokami. Illuminara je šla po zidu navzdol, položila dlan na kamen ob razpoki in držala skalo pri miru štiri minute, kolikor je glina potrebovala, da se je prijela. Vedela je, da bi štirideset parov rok in vedro gline brez nje opravilo enako, pa je vseeno ostala, en par rok med mnogimi. Nihče se ji ni zahvalil. Govorili so le: *Drži, drži*, in držala je.

Ob devetem zvonu se je zadnji vagon Pete povzpel iz kanjona, prebivalec Hollow Towna je stal pri vsaki kretnici, vrste svetilk pa so svetleče prečkale senco. Kljun in Peta sta bila na oddaljeni ravnici spet eno mesto, eno uro pred vročino. Za njima je na kretničnih drogovih v kanjonu ostalo prižganih sedemnajst svetilk, ki so jih tja obesili Hodci in jih niso hoteli sneti.
Prvi voz na novih tirnicah je bil vodni voz Hollow Towna, vagoni Kljuna z žitom pa so mu odstopili pol dolžine, kakor se umakneš nekomu, ki je plačal.

Tisti večer je na drugi strani Razpoke zazvonil večerni zvon. Ob mizi Sveta je na koncu klopi stal nov stol, na njem pa je sedela Kesa s seznamom na kolenih. Thaw je prebrala dvanajst imen Ostalih, nato pa odprla drugi seznam, ki ji ga je Kesa dala, ne da bi jo kdo prosil.

**Wenna Thaw**  
Hollow Town me je prosil, naj jih berem ob mraku, da ne bomo mesto, ki jih je pozabilo šteti. Dvanajst. Nato dvanajst.

Illuminara je hodila na koncu Pete, v istem koraku, v roki pa držala dlan desetletne deklice, ki jo je tja položila brez razprave. Pred njimi je bilo nebo barve modrice, ki se celi, mesto pa je hodilo proti njemu v enem kosu, skupaj z zapuščenimi med svetilkami.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara spozna, da sta Pravilo Orrin Kella in zavrnitev Hollow Towna žalost v dveh nasprotnih oblikah, nato svobodno izbrano spravo obeh skupnosti poveže z enim preverljivim fizikalnim načelom, tako da mesto prečka kanjon, ne da bi ga kdo nesel, zapuščeni dobijo trajen glas, slišana pa sta oba seznama imen.
